openUiAnatomy: no published Open UI alert anatomy — union of shadcn Alert/AlertTitle/AlertDescription, salt-ds Banner/BannerContent/BannerActions (composes StatusIndicator), M3's 'banners' token family (basic + rich variants, standard/vibrant color roles). Canonical name is shadcn's 'alert'; Salt and M3 both call the same component 'banner' (docs/COMPONENTS.md Feedback & status table).

behavior.pattern: non-modal, non-dismissing-by-default status message region. No source system implements built-in open/close state or an auto-dismiss timer — dismissal, if any, is always a consumer-composed onClick on a close/action button (Salt's own 'Dismissible' story manages open state with external useState). The only cross-system behavior axis is WHICH ARIA role announces it, mirroring Spinner's role finding but with a twist: Salt has NO default role at all (a real, sourced absence, not a gap in our research) while shadcn hardcodes one.
behavior.chassis: skeleton/alert.tsx — written from the template's part union; inherits from no design system

rows.note: M3 rich only (_md-comp-banners-rich.scss image.size 80dp, image.shape corner-none) — a leading image is an alternative to the leading icon. Salt (icon only, via StatusIndicator) and shadcn (icon-only, arbitrary <svg> child) have no image-leading-element concept at all.

shadcn: dedicated AlertTitle part (col-start-2, font-medium, line-clamp-1). M3 rich: dedicated title-text token family (title-text-height/top-space/bottom-space, emphasized body-medium typescale). Salt: NO dedicated title part — Banner/BannerContent expose no title subcomponent; a bold first line is achieved purely by consumer content formatting (... inside BannerContent, see banner.stories.tsx 'Issue'/'MultipleLines' stories) — same class of finding as Calendar's today-marker: three systems, three different answers to 'how do I emphasize the headline,' one of them (Salt) not a structural answer at all.

Salt: dedicated BannerActions wrapper (optional). shadcn (new-york-v4 canonical): NO dedicated actions wrapper — action buttons are placed as arbitrary children with no distinct data-slot hook (all new-york-v4 demo/example files only show icon+title+description, never an action button). Supplementary evidence this is still a real shadcn-family pattern: the sibling 'radix' base variant in the SAME monorepo (registry/bases/radix/ui/alert.tsx) ships a dedicated `data-slot="alert-action"` element, used in examples/radix/alert-action.tsx. M3: basic + rich both have an actions token family (leading/trailing/top/bottom spacing, between-space).

M3 only has a FIRST-CLASS dedicated close affordance: _md-comp-banners.scss close-button-color/-focused/-hovered/-pressed tokens plus _md-comp-banners-basic.scss actions-close-button-space (8px, 4px mobile) — a distinct part, not folded into the generic actions group. Salt and shadcn both achieve dismiss by placing an ordinary close-labeled Button/icon-button INSIDE the generic actions area (Salt: banner.stories.tsx 'Dismissible'/'Interactive' stories put <Button aria-label="close"><CloseIcon/></Button> inside BannerActions; shadcn: same composition convention, no dedicated part) — a real structural difference in how the same dismiss capability is expressed, not a coverage gap.

DECLARED COMPOSITION (same pattern as calendar.template.json's slot.composes): alert's action buttons and close button compose the registry's own `button` component (already built) — Salt literally renders a Button in BannerActions, shadcn's sibling AlertAction wraps a Button, M3's actions are token-described as buttons. The status/leading icon composes a future registry icon-set component. Both render as neutral placeholders in this skeleton (a plain SVG glyph for the icon, a plain <button> for actions/close) rather than importing skeleton/button.tsx directly, keeping this component's build self-contained — the composed components' own matrices will replace these approximations.

the alert/banner ROOT itself has no keyboard pattern, no tabindex, no click handler in any source — identical across all three. Only its composed action/close buttons are interactive (Tab moves focus through them per Salt's own accessibility.mdx keyboard-interactions doc); their states belong to the composed button component, out of scope here.

Salt: NO default role attribute at all — Banner.tsx sets none; Salt's own accessibility.mdx instructs the consumer to apply role="alert" (to interrupt) or role="status" (to notify) THEMSELVES per use case, with a documented caveat that role="status" has known screen-reader announcement issues for dynamically-inserted content. This is a real, sourced absence, not a research gap — recorded as switched OFF for Salt. shadcn: role="alert" hardcoded in alert.tsx, always, not a prop. M3: [R] no live component in this tokens-only clone; treated as role="status" per the general APG banner/live-region convention, not grepped from code.

shared invariant: no source system implements built-in open/close state or an auto-dismiss timer. Salt's own 'Dismissible' banner.stories.tsx example manages `open` with an external useState + onClick on the composed close Button — the same consumer-owned pattern any shadcn/M3 build would need. Nothing to switch per column; recorded once.

Salt: 4-value ValidationStatus enum (info/error/warning/success), Banner's `status` prop, default "info". shadcn: 2-value variant enum (default/destructive) — the same tone-coverage gap already found in Button. M3: OFF — confirmed by direct grep of every banner-family token file (_md-comp-banner.scss, _md-comp-banners.scss, _md-comp-banners-basic.scss, _md-comp-banners-rich.scss): none defines a semantic status/tone axis at all, only a standard/vibrant EMPHASIS axis (see prop.emphasis). M3 has a general sys-color `error`/`error-container` role elsewhere in the design system, but it is not part of the banner component's own token family, so mapping it here would exceed this matrix's sourcing discipline — a real structural divergence, the marquee finding of this matrix (see ALERT-MATRIX.md Findings).

Salt: `variant` prop, primary (default, always-neutral container) / secondary (tone-tinted background). shadcn: OFF — new-york-v4's alert has no separate emphasis/intensity axis; its `variant` prop IS the tone axis (default/destructive), and background never changes regardless of variant (see style.root.background finding) — a real non-variation, not an omission. M3: standard (surface-container, on-surface text) / vibrant (primary-container, on-primary-container text), _md-comp-banners.scss — a pure decorative-intensity choice, notably NOT status-driven since M3 has no status axis to begin with.
consumer-owned glyph content (status icon or arbitrary icon); Salt fixes it to the status via StatusIndicator, shadcn/M3 leave the specific icon fully up to the consumer
consumer-owned headline text, where the system has a title part (see structure.title)

consumer-owned body content; all three sources accept arbitrary children/nodes here (Salt: BannerContent's required children; shadcn: AlertDescription, optional per-instance but structurally always available; M3: supporting/body-text)
consumer-owned action buttons, where the system has an actions part (see structure.actions)
consumer-owned close affordance, first-class only in M3 (see structure.close)

shared invariant: the alert/banner root has no hover/focus/active/disabled rule anywhere in any source — confirmed no such rule in Banner.css or alert.tsx's cva variants, and no interaction-state tokens in any M3 banner token file. Any interactive states belong entirely to the composed action/close buttons, owned by the future button component's own matrix, not this one.

shown at emphasis=primary/default/standard (each system's least-emphasized container). DECLARED DEFERRAL, same limitation as Spinner's size/Button's tone grid: only the default emphasis level resolves here; the tone-tinted / vibrant levels are the extra style.root.background@emphasis row below, the same 'one representative non-default axis cell' pattern button.template.json established.

the emphasis axis's non-default value, at the default tone (Salt: info; M3 has no tone so 'vibrant' is tone-agnostic by definition). shadcn is OFF here deliberately — new-york-v4's alert background never changes regardless of variant, a real non-variation (see prop.emphasis note), not a missing cell. Selector unions each system's own attribute vocabulary for its non-default emphasis value, same generalized-selector pattern as button.template.json's style.root.background@secondary row (never a bare hardcoded single-system selector).

shown at the default tone. Salt's border color is status-driven (border-color = the SAME palette-{status} value used for the icon, see style.icon.color — Banner.css: --banner-borderColor -> status-{status}-borderColor). shadcn's border color is a FIXED neutral `border` token that never varies by variant/tone — Alert's cva classes never touch border-color, a real non-variation confirmed by reading alertVariants directly. M3 is OFF: no border/outline token exists anywhere in the banner token family (_md-comp-banner*.scss) — M3's banners are color-fill only, a genuine structural absence, not a gap.

Salt: --salt-size-fixed-100 = 1px, density-invariant. shadcn: Tailwind's default `border` = 1px (undeclared token, per foundations/border-style.md). M3: explicitly set to 0 (not left off) — since `base` sets border-style:solid for cross-system layout convenience, leaving M3's width truly absent would let the browser's initial `medium` (~3px) border-width render an unwanted visible border; 0 is the honest way to express 'no border' without that side effect.

shown at the default tone. Salt is the ONLY system where the icon's color is genuinely distinct from (and independent of) the body text's color — StatusIndicator resolves to palette-{status}, while the root's own text stays a neutral content-primary-foreground regardless of status. shadcn ([&>svg]:text-current, i.e. inherits the root's own color) and M3 (standard-icon-color/vibrant-icon-color both equal that variant's own text color role) both tie icon color to the SAME role as the body text — aliased here to the same slot as style.root.color for those two systems, not a separate token, and that convergence is recorded as a finding.

Salt: spacing-50 (block) spacing-100 (inline), by density. shadcn: py-3 px-4 = 12px 16px, fixed. M3: rich schema's top/bottom/leading/trailing-space = 12px uniformly (the with-image-leading-space=20px override is out of scope, same style of scope trim as Calendar's locale row).

gap between the leading icon/image and the content column. Salt: spacing-75, by density. shadcn: has-[>svg]:gap-x-3 = 12px (rendered here as a flex gap; shadcn's real layout is CSS grid columns, a structural approximation declared, not silent). M3 rich: icon-text-space = 4px.

Salt: palette-corner (rounded-edition pin, same as Calendar/Button) = curve-150, by density. shadcn: --radius-lg = 10px. M3: corner-extra-large = 28px (rich schema's `shape` token; the 'basic' variant's square option, corner-none, is out of scope under this matrix's rich-schema pin — see ALERT-MATRIX.md Edition pin).

Salt: calc(size-base + spacing-100), by density (Banner.css). shadcn: OFF — content-driven, no min-height token anywhere in alert.tsx, a real gap. M3: OFF under the rich-schema pin (rich has no single container min-height token); the 'basic' schema DOES define one (height: 56px, two-lines: 64px) but basic is out of scope here — declared, not silently dropped.

the body/description type. Salt: --salt-text-* body role, by density (Open Sans, weight-regular). shadcn: text-sm (0.875rem/1.25rem), no shadcn type-scale foundation exists (per foundations/typography.md) so this is read directly off the component's own Tailwind classes. M3: body-medium (0.875rem/1.25rem, weight-regular, Roboto — self-hosted per this pipeline's existing Calendar/Button precedent for M3's 'plain' typeface role, which this tokens-only clone never spells out as a literal family string).

shown at the default emphasis/tone. Salt: content-primary-foreground (neutral, does NOT vary by status — a real non-variation). shadcn: text-card-foreground (default variant). M3: on-surface (standard variant).

shadcn: font-medium (weight 500), same 0.875rem/1.25rem size as the body (AlertTitle sets no independent font-size). M3 rich: title-text uses the EMPHASIZED body-medium typescale (md-sys-typescale-emphasized, weight-medium=500, same 0.875rem/1.25rem size/line-height as regular body-medium — the emphasis here is a real, CSS-expressible weight difference, 500 vs 400, not merely a variable-font-axis effect). Salt is OFF — no distinct title font, because there is no distinct title part (see structure.title).

shadcn is the ONLY system with a distinct (muted) description color, separate from the title/root color — text-muted-foreground on AlertDescription vs text-card-foreground on the root/title. Salt and M3 are both OFF here: neither tokenizes a separate description color — Salt's BannerContent sets no color of its own (inherits content-primary-foreground from the root, same value as style.root.color) and M3's rich body-text-color resolves to the SAME on-surface role as its title-text-color in the standard variant — both real convergences, not gaps.

Non-default tone. Mirrors Salt's OWN mechanism exactly: Banner.css declares `border-color: var(--banner-borderColor)` once and then reassigns that one custom property per status (`.saltBanner-error { --banner-borderColor: var(--salt-status-error-borderColor) }`), including the secondary-emphasis background (`.saltBanner-secondary.saltBanner-error`). Modelled here as an indirection slot the base rows consume, rather than duplicating every tone-varying property as its own row. ADDED IN VALIDATION: the first generated pass declared prop.tone with four values but shipped no CSS that varied by tone, so three of Salt's four tones rendered identically to info - a silent fallback (CLAUDE.md rule 3), caught in the render check, not by the generator.
Non-default tone - see style.root.tone@error.
Non-default tone - see style.root.tone@error.

shadcn's only non-default tone. Unlike Salt (border + icon) and unlike its own background (bg-card is IDENTICAL in both variants), shadcn's destructive variant recolours TEXT: `text-destructive` on the root/title/icon plus `*:data-[slot=alert-description]:text-destructive/90` on the description. Same indirection approach as the Salt tone rows above.
